content:
A Russian strike drone hit a five-storey residential apartment building in the town of Dymer, north of Kyiv, overnight into Sunday, collapsing flats from the first to the fifth floors and killing at least two people, Ukrainian officials said.

The strike, which set the building ablaze, left four people injured and fifteen residents unaccounted for, including two children, as emergency crews worked through the rubble on Sunday morning. A nearby kindergarten and a local shop were also damaged, according to the Kyiv regional administration.

Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv Regional Military Administration, announced the toll on Telegram after rescuers recovered a second body from the debris. "The death toll from the enemy attack in Dymer has risen to two. Rescuers have recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble," he said, according to Ukrinform.

One of those killed was an 18-year-old young man, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said. Among the four injured was a teenager born in 2010 who suffered multiple shrapnel wounds to his arm and was taken to hospital, a 22-year-old woman treated at the scene for cuts to her foot, and a man born in 1977 who was hospitalised with a head injury. A child was also among the injured.

Rescuers evacuated nine people from the building, including one child, but the search for the missing continued into the afternoon. Ukrainian police said fifteen people were listed as missing, including an 11-year-old girl and a seven-year-old boy, while the emergency service said at least seven people may still be trapped beneath the debris. Psychologists from the emergency service were working at the site with survivors and relatives, and the death toll could still rise.

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned the strike, the latest in a punishing run of Russian attacks on the Kyiv region in a single week. On Friday, a large-scale missile assault on the capital killed seven people, injured 17 and damaged key bridges across the Dnipro River, according to the Kyiv Post. On Saturday morning, a further aerial attack injured two men aged 63 and 67 and damaged private homes across the capital's Podil, Holosiivskyi and Solomianskyi districts.

The same week, a Russian missile strike on Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, killed a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman and wounded 60 people, in an attack officials said deliberately targeted rescue workers as they responded to an earlier blast. That strike is covered in [Global Wire's report on the Kryvyi Rih attack](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/ar/articles/russian-strike-kryvyi-rih-zelenskyy-hometown-november-2026).

The attacks have come as diplomatic efforts to end the war continue in parallel. The United States envoy Jared Kushner said this week that talks on ending the war had made progress, as reported in [Global Wire's coverage of the negotiations](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/ar/articles/kushner-ukraine-talks-progress-zelenskyy-missiles-november-2026), days after the first trilateral summit between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia in Shenzhen. But on the ground, Ukrainian officials say the bombardment of civilian areas has only intensified, and Kyiv's need for additional air defences has become more urgent than ever.

Russia has not commented on the Dymer strike. Moscow has repeatedly said its forces target only military objectives, a claim contradicted by the pattern of destroyed apartment blocks, hospitals and schools documented across Ukraine since the full-scale invasion began.

As of Sunday afternoon, the search and rescue operation in Dymer was still under way, with heavy machinery clearing the collapsed section of the building floor by floor. Officials warned that the number of dead and injured was being updated continuously, and that families of the missing were waiting at the scene for news.

The photograph accompanying this article shows a Kyiv apartment building damaged in a Russian drone strike on 12 November 2026. For the latest reporting on the Dymer attack, see [the Kyiv Independent's coverage](https://kyivindependent.com/apartment-building-destroyed-in-kyiv-oblast-following-russian-drone-attack/).
summary: A Russian drone hit a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, overnight into Sunday, killing two people and injuring four. Fifteen residents, including two children, remain missing as rescuers dig through the rubble.
title: Russian drone strike destroys apartment block near Kyiv, killing two as rescuers search for 15 missing
